newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Vasseur hits EU farm package proposals.
newsitem.headline: France's Vasseur hits EU farm package proposals.

text.p: France will not accept the 1997/98 farm pricing package drafted by the European Commission in its present form, especially a proposal to cut direct aid payments to grain producers, farm minister Phillipe Vasseur said on Wednesday.
Vasseur also urged the European Commission to propose a new set-aside rate for the 1998 grain harvest as quickly as possible.

"France will not relent on the set-aside rate, nor on a reduction of compensatory payments and it will oppose any pricing package if these two conditions are not met," Vasseur told the National Assembly.
The European Commission wants to cut aid payments to cereal farmers by 1.4 billion Ecus to fund extra aid for beef farmers hit by the mad cow crisis.
The Commission made a similar proposal last Summer but had to drop it as it failed to attract enough support from member states.

The new proposal drew strong criticism from European Union farm ministers meeting in Brussels last week. They said the payments agreed in 1992 to compensate farmers for price and production cuts were permanent and could not be reduced.
But EU farm Commissioner Franz Fischler said the cuts were needed to curb grain output that surged 15 percent to a record 202 million tonnes in 1996.
Vasseur told the assembly the proposal to cut aid payments to grain producers was not justified, particularly as it was aimed at solving EU budgetary problems.

EU farm ministers, especially France, the largest grain producer in the Union, want the Commission to come up promptly with a proposal on a new set-aside rate for the 1998 harvest. They are worried that because of rising grain production, the current rate of five percent may be increased. --Paris newsroom +33 1 4221 5432
